admission.justification: Three skip exits exist: a non-injective pairing, a marker/reference mismatch on a renumbered side, and non-decodable Markdown on a renumbered side. Two witnesses are stored: the marker-incomplete fixture pins the whole legacy merge with its reason, while the collision fixture pins the helper-level injectivity guard only (_assign_numbers returns None) without exercising the whole merge. A future change that aligns an ambiguous card instead of skipping fails before it lands. The original two-exit claim is retained in origin.handoff.evidence below as dated Worker provenance.

applicability: Both-changed cards whose pairing is ambiguous or whose renumbered side has marker/reference mismatch.
conditions: The skip reason is recorded for the crossing report.
The card then merges by the pre-R66 rules with no alignment.
exclusions: Cards that align: pairing success plus marker eligibility on every renumbered side. A paired card that fails the later marker-eligibility check still skips, so pairing success alone is not sufficient.

evidence: Rationale: the only two exits that skip alignment are a non-injective pairing (which would give one number to two references) and a marker/reference count mismatch on a side that would be renumbered; both return the reason string, and _align_cards records it in skippedCards while the card merges exactly as today. The mismatch compares pre-remap numbers on each side, so it cannot misfire on the renumbering itself. Observed: rule-7 skip tests plus skippedCards assertions in the report-seam tests; the validator is untouched.

statement: Rule 7 no-guess: duplicate-number pairing or marker/reference mismatch on a renumbered side merges the card without alignment exactly as today, with the reason recorded
